Algal_Leaf_Spot.quote: Algal leaf spot is most visible when it affects leaves

Damage to the plant is greatest when twigs and branches are affected. The alga enters through a small crack or crevice in the bark. The bark in that area thickens and cracks as a canker forms that eventually can girdle the branch, killing it.
Algal diseases caused by Cephaleuros virescens on durian trees are characterized by the appearance of orange, rust-colored velutinous spots on the upper surfaces of leaves, twigs, and branches.

Allocaridara_Attack.quote: The grub and mature one suck the nutrients from the bud, so the leaf is crooked and finally falls.
The grub produces the white grease to cover its body and leave it on the leaf.
